➕ Capture a mistake

🔍 Pattern diagnosis

Based only on entries recorded in this lab. Use patterns to choose what to practise next, not as a judgement of ability.

Weekly review protocol
  1. Choose the most frequent error category.
  2. Re-derive or explain the underlying concept without notes.
  3. Solve 3 fresh problems on the same idea.
  4. Revisit this entry after 1, 3, 7 and 14 days.
  5. Mark it mastered only after solving a fresh problem independently.

v44 Stability & Feature Status

Theme animation is OFF by default to reduce distraction and lag. In Settings, enable automatic switching if wanted; the minimum interval is now 120 seconds (2 minutes). Use “Switch theme now” for a manual change.

  • AI tutor and research: UI/API wiring is present, but it needs your own valid provider endpoint, model, API key, internet, permissions and possibly a backend proxy. Research citations are shown only when returned by the provider; verify them.
  • PYQs: the finder links to official paper/answer-key repositories and topic searches. This is not a bundled, fully verified question bank; verify the paper code and final answer key.
  • Notifications: reminders while the page is open differ from closed-app push notifications. The latter require native APK/Median plus FCM/OneSignal or equivalent server-side setup.
  • Backup: local recovery/export is included. Automatic writes to Android files and cloud sync are not guaranteed without device permissions and configured backend/RLS.
  • PDF: preview and external-open/download fallbacks are included; test on the installed Android WebView and use an external PDF reader if the preview is blank.
  • English: language controls cover common labels/new panels; older hard-coded legacy text may remain untranslated.

Reliability & Integration Hub

Single-file integration layer. AI web research uses Gemini with Google Search grounding, and native push needs Median configuration. Local recovery works only while this app's storage remains available; keep a downloaded backup too.

AI research with citations (Gemini + Google Search)

Uses the Gemini API key from Gemini Ultra → Setup. Answers are grounded in Google Search and list their sources; verify anything important on the official site.

Needs a Gemini API key (Gemini Ultra → Setup).

Official PYQ & answer-key finder

Only official repositories are labelled official. Questions/solutions are not copied into this app; confirm paper code, shift and final answer key on the source page. Search filters help locate material but do not prove a question's answer.

Recovery & backup

Automatic IndexedDB snapshots of app storage are saved periodically on this device. This is not an Android file-system backup and cannot survive every app-data clear/uninstall.

Restore replaces matching localStorage keys. Export first. Cloud sync requires a working signed-in Supabase setup and correct RLS/table schema.

PHASE 11 · CLOUD SYNC DIAGNOSTICS

☁️ Supabase Cloud Sync Lab

Diagnose the connection before trusting cloud backups. This page does not silently upload, delete, or restore your study data.

Safety: Use only your Supabase project URL and publishable/anon key. Never paste a service-role/secret key. Keep this HTML private. The diagnostic test is read-only; a successful network test does not prove that sign-in, RLS, or uploads work.

1. Check the project connection

Enter the URL and publishable/anon key in Backup / Settings first. The test below uses those existing fields and sends no password or study data.

Not tested yet.

2. Expected database table and Row Level Security

The current cloud backup code expects public.jee_user_data with user_id (UUID), data (JSONB), and updated_at (timestamp). If the table does not exist or RLS policies differ, uploads may fail. Review this SQL before running it in your own Supabase SQL Editor.

This SQL is a suggested starting point, not an automatic migration. Review it first. Do not disable RLS or grant access to anon/public.

3. Safe troubleshooting guide

“Failed to fetch”

Often means the browser could not complete the request: check internet, exact project URL, browser/network restrictions, and whether the project is reachable. This message alone does not identify the cause.

401 / invalid API key

Recheck that the key belongs to this exact Supabase project and is a publishable/anon key. Do not share the key in screenshots or chats.

Email confirmation required

Open the confirmation email and complete verification, then sign in again. Also check spam and the project's email/auth settings.

Table not found / schema error

Check that the table name and column names match the expected schema above.

403 / RLS policy error

Confirm the user is signed in and the policies restrict each row to auth.uid() = user_id. Never fix this by making the table public.

4. Before trusting cloud sync

  1. Run the project connection test.
  2. Confirm email and sign in using Backup / Settings.
  3. Check table access.
  4. Export a fresh local JSON backup.
  5. Upload once, then verify the saved row in Supabase and test downloading it.
  6. Only after a successful restore test should you treat cloud backup as reliable.

This page cannot verify the private Supabase dashboard configuration automatically. Cloud sync status must be confirmed by actual successful operations.

📦 Android Packaging Kit

Prepare this private HTML study app for a Capacitor-based Android wrapper.
Phase 13

This page is a packaging guide and checklist. It does not compile an APK, upload your app, or verify cloud sync.

1. App files

Keep the latest HTML file as www/index.html. Keep a separate backup before replacing it.

2. Build environment

Capacitor requires Node.js/npm and an Android build environment. An APK is not generated by opening this HTML in Chrome.

3. Package identity

Use a unique reverse-domain application ID. Changing it after installation may make Android treat it as a different app.

4. Release safety

Build commands

npm init -y
npm install @capacitor/core
npm install -D @capacitor/cli
npm install @capacitor/android
npx cap init
npx cap add android
npx cap sync android
npx cap open android
Run these in a terminal inside the project folder. During npx cap init, use your chosen app name and application ID; set web directory to www in the Capacitor config.

Complete the checks only after you have actually tested them.

Important limits

  • This page does not create a signed APK or AAB.
  • Local browser storage may behave differently in an Android WebView; verify persistence and backup/restore after installation.
  • Do not put Supabase service-role keys, private API keys, or other secrets in the HTML, config, or APK.
  • Cloud sync is not considered working until authentication, database policies, and read/write flows have been tested with separate user accounts.
  • Do not publish the APK or upload personal backup files if the app is intended to remain private.

🛠️ Android Build & Installation Support

Phase 14 · A guided route from your private HTML project to a testable Android APK.
Build helper

Important: this guide does not compile an APK inside the HTML app. It helps you prepare a project and follow a build workflow. A successful build and phone installation must be verified separately.

Route A — GitHub cloud build

  1. Create a private GitHub repository.
  2. Extract the Phase 14 ZIP and upload the project files, including .github/workflows/build-android.yml.
  3. Open the repository's Actions tab and enable workflows if asked.
  4. Run the “Build Android debug APK” workflow or push a commit.
  5. Open the successful workflow run and download the jee-study-os-debug-apk artifact.
  6. Download the APK to your Android phone, review Android's install prompt, and install only your own build.

Keep the repository private. A debug APK is for testing, not a production release.

Route B — Android Studio

  1. Extract the project on a computer with Node.js/npm and Android Studio installed.
  2. Run npm ci (or npm install if no lock file exists).
  3. Run npx cap sync android.
  4. Open the Android project with npx cap open android.
  5. Build a debug APK from Android Studio and install it on a test phone.

Build checklist

0/6Checks marked
0%Checklist progress

Common build failures

  • Workflow missing: verify the exact path .github/workflows/build-android.yml.
  • Gradle/Java error: check the workflow log and keep Java version consistent with the Android Gradle Plugin.
  • Web assets missing: verify the latest HTML is at www/index.html, then run npx cap sync android.
  • Install blocked: use Android's install prompt only for an APK you built and trust; review device settings rather than disabling protections broadly.
  • App opens but data is missing: browser localStorage and app WebView storage may be separate. Test migration/backup explicitly.

Commands for Android Studio route

npm ci
npx cap sync android
npx cap open android

Security and privacy

  • Do not add Supabase service-role keys, private API keys, or passwords to HTML, GitHub files, or APK assets.
  • Do not upload JSON backups containing personal study records to a public repository.
  • Use GitHub Actions artifacts for testing; avoid committing built APKs unless you deliberately want them in the repository.
  • Cloud sync must be tested independently; building an APK does not prove authentication or RLS is secure.

Test & migrate

Critical: Chrome website storage and an installed Android app's WebView storage are normally separate. Installing the APK will not automatically move your Chrome study records. Do not clear Chrome data until you have verified a backup.

📱 APK smoke-test checklist

Tick each check only after testing it on the actual installed APK.

🧭 Migration safety steps

  1. In Chrome, open the original app and create a fresh JSON backup.
  2. Copy the backup to a private, safe location. It may contain sensitive study data or settings.
  3. Install and test the APK without deleting the original Chrome app or its site data.
  4. Use only a documented import/restore function that understands the backup's format.
  5. Verify sample records, totals, settings and dates in the APK.
  6. Keep the original backup until you have confirmed the migrated data is complete.

This page does not transfer data across app sandboxes by itself and does not upload data to a server.

📦 Reliable Data Import & Export
Phase 16 · Versioned backups, preview, duplicate-aware merge, and safer restore.
Local-first

  
Safety first: backups may contain private study data, settings, or credentials. Keep files private. This tool processes files in your browser and does not upload them. Export a fresh backup before importing anything.

 

 

  
1. Create a versioned backup
Exports browser localStorage as a versioned JSON archive. It preserves each stored value as its original string.

  
2. Inspect backup before import
No file inspected yet.

 

 
3. Import options
Merge keeps any destination key that already exists and imports only missing keys. Replace updates only keys present in the selected backup; it does not clear unrelated browser data.



 
4. Import report
No import has been run in this session.

 
Compatibility and recovery notes
  • Backups use format jee-study-os-backup with a numeric schema version.
  • Older or unknown formats are rejected rather than silently guessed.
  • Merge skips keys already present; replace overwrites only keys included in the archive.
  • Values are imported as stored strings. This tool does not merge inside complex JSON objects or reconcile conflicts within a key.
  • Chrome and an installed APK may have separate storage. This export/import workflow can help transfer a backup manually, but the destination must support this same tool and storage access.
  • Do not import a backup you do not trust. A malicious or malformed file should not be treated as safe just because it is JSON.

🔐 How the integration works

  
    
   
  • Incorrect / partial / skipped attempt → candidate: created from the Phase 19 Question Bank attempt log.
    • 
   
  • Create mistake record: adds a draft-like entry to the existing Mistake Intelligence store using its known field structure. You can edit details later in Mistake Intelligence.
    • 
   
  • Create revision card: adds a recall prompt to the existing Personalised Revision store. The prompt asks you to re-solve the question and explain the key idea.
    • 
   
  • Duplicate protection: this engine checks question-attempt IDs against its own created-action registry and uses source IDs for revision cards. It does not auto-create records during scanning.
    • 
   
  • Local-only: all actions happen in this browser's local storage. Export a backup before making large changes.
